summary: baseline-recipe: FAIL: sampled first tokens vs the server's own log-probabilities: mean TV 0.0702, expected 0.0189, excess +0.0513 (95% CI +0.0075 to +0.1205, margin 0.02) over 11 prompts x 256 seeds; 71 of 5888 draws outside the kept tokens
limitations: self-consistency: shows that the server's draws follow its own top-20 log-probabilities under these settings; whether those log-probabilities match the baseline's is the teacher-forced check's job (quality score)
max_tokens 1: the first generated token only (prefill), not later positions or longer contexts
the listed log-probabilities must be raw (log-softmax before temperature, top-k and top-p, vLLM's default); a server that returns processed ones reads as a wrong sampler
tokens are matched by id (vLLM's return_token_ids and return_tokens_as_token_ids)
min_p, repetition_penalty not sent: read as off, but a server that applies its own default (vLLM applies generation_config.json) then draws from another distribution; send every sampling field
concurrency 16: a batched engine's logits change with the batch, so draws taken alongside other requests need not follow the log-probabilities of one alone
top_k with top_p: SGLang takes top-p over the whole distribution, Hugging Face and vLLM over the top-k tokens; a prompt counts only when both keep the same tokens

the margin bounds the mean excess TV, not the sampler's own error: the excess grows about with the square of a small error, so a sampler a few hundredths of probability off can still PASS (256 seeds x 32 prompts)

data.reason: 71 of 5888 draws (1.21%, 95% CI 0.96% to 1.52%) are tokens these settings remove (limit 0.5%); min_p, repetition_penalty not sent and read as off: a server that applies its own default for them (vLLM applies generation_config.json) would also give this

dropped_why.logprobs_unstable: the top-20 token ids changed between two identical requests
